title: adm delivered as base64(HTML) is decoded exactly once and renders as markup
specRef: specs/012-creative-preview-repair/contracts/creative-preview.md §1 (classification order: base64 is decoded exactly once, the decoded body is the creative); https://github.com/InteractiveAdvertisingBureau/openrtb2.x/blob/403cbba542de3a5d9cfcccd0a34e74b01b79a9f1/2.6.md#objectbid does not forbid a base64-wrapped adm string — the wrapping is an SSP-side convention, not a protocol violation.
specNotes: Core never decodes bid.adm; it validates the base64 text as an opaque string (no VAST/native shape, no obfuscation pattern) and must produce no error from the encoding alone.

The encoded run is 240 base64 characters, held well under the 500-character BASE64_MIN_RUN the static entropy scanner (packages/core/behavior/rules/static.js) uses before it ever inspects entropy — this case is not exercising that scanner.

public/modules/inspector/creative-classify.js classifies a base64 body by decoding exactly one round and re-classifying the decoded text; a plain HTML document decodes to kind "markup" and is the only kind the preview frames.
